# ethereum-optimism/infra Daily Update (Mar 23, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on enhancing CircleCI test statistics by mapping flaky test markers to structured statuses. A new issue was opened regarding missing TLS support for WebSocket upstreams in proxyd.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

*   **Improved CircleCI Test Statistics**
    *   Added a helper function `mapFlakyStatus()` to detect `FLAKY_FAIL:` and `FLAKY_PASS:` prefixes in CircleCI test skip messages.
    *   Updated `fetchTestMetadata()` to include flaky-marked skipped tests, rather than filtering all skipped tests, providing more granular test status reporting ([#576](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/576)).

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
No new pull requests were opened today.

## CLOSED ISSUES

*   **Flaky Test Resolution**
    *   The `TestSupernodeSameTimestampInvalidTransitive` test was closed as fixed, with analysis indicating it has not failed in the last 43 consecutive runs, suggesting the flakiness has been resolved ([#19570](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19570)).

## NEW ISSUES

*   **Proxyd TLS Support for WebSockets**
    *   A new issue was opened to address the lack of TLS support for WebSocket upstreams in proxyd, noting that backend TLS configuration is currently only applied to HTTP transport ([#577](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/577)).

## ACTIVE ISSUES

*   **Kona Guest Panics Deserializing chainList.json** ([#19654](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19654))
    *   A new link was saved to a Notion page detailing the "kona proofs panic: Failed to read chain list," indicating ongoing investigation into the issue where the kona guest program panics during Cannon VM execution when deserializing the superchain registry chain list.

*   **Flake: TestCLELDivergence — L2CLB unsafe head did not expose target block** ([#19681](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19681))
    *   Discussion continues on the `TestCLELDivergence` flaky test. The latest comments suggest that the observed reset is likely part of the initial derivation pipeline lifecycle and not necessarily a signal of an issue during EL sync. It was noted that the test comment might be incorrect regarding the source of the reset, and there might not be a reset bug. Proposed mitigations include waiting for op-nodes to complete their initial derivation reset before running the divergence test or using `require.Eventually` for multiple checks.

*   **Interop Phase 3: Removing Chains From Shared Dispute Games** ([#19692](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19692))
    *   A question was raised regarding the necessity and implications of removing chains from shared dispute games, seeking clarification on the use cases and whether it means chains are actually removed from the interop set.

*   **CGT chains and shared dispute games** ([#19711](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19711))
    *   A comment highlighted a potential workaround needed for CGT chains to enable the correct predeploys in the interop fork, specifically concerning the SuperchainETHBridge/ETHLiquidity contracts.

*   **[tracking]: Review kona-interop block hash oracle** ([#18288](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18288))
    *   An update was provided on adding a test for the `OracleInteropProvider::header_by_number` in `kona-proof-interop`. A fixture-based integration test was opened ([#19726](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/19726)) after a full acceptance test proved too time-consuming. The new fixture uses real OP Mainnet state/storage trie proof data to force the full production path and runs significantly faster. Once merged, the old action test (`TestInteropFaultProofs_DeepCanonicalBlockQuery`) can be removed.

*   **Consider overlap between CGT and ETHLiquidity contracts** ([#19461](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19461))
    *   A comment noted the overlap between CGT and ETHLiquidity contracts, suggesting it's a worthy consideration when scoping the case for CGT chains joining interop.
